name: Tiller & Persinger 2002: time-reversed Thomas pattern, right (5 min)
summary: The 849-point 'Thomas' table played backwards (pulses speeding up instead of slowing down), at 3 ms per point over the right parietotemporal region, 1 uT for 5 min: the comparison configuration that Tiller & Persinger 2002 reported as less effective than the forward pattern for left-sided presences.
notes: Same table, timing, coils and intensity as persinger-tiller-2002-thomas-right, with the point order reversed; Buckner 2015 describes the lab's reverse Thomas file the same way ('proceeds from 6 Hz to 25 Hz'). Tiller & Persinger reported it less effective than the forward pattern for left-sided presences; with the same points and energy in the opposite time order, it is the forward file's active control. The forward table is Table 1 of US 6,234,953 (Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger), 849 points, which the lab replayed at 3 ms per point (Buckner 2015; Murugan 2013); with a 3-ms pause after each pass (the rat optimum of Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999) one pass lasts 2.55 s, in which 18 pulses speed up from about 5 to 12 per second (the lab's '6 to 25 Hz' labels do not follow from the table). Reversing the point order also mirrors each pulse in time, as a reversed point file does. Sites T8 and TP8 are an inference; the left channels stay silent. A 5-s fade is added at start and end. For a blinded test, have someone else pick this file, the forward file or a sham. n = 12, one lab, no independent replication of the forward-versus-reversed difference. Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Blindfolded or with opaque goggles in a quiet, dark room; report the moment and side of anything felt.
schedule: One 5-min block, at most once a week.
source: Tiller & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:26 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11883572/ ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (849 points at 3 ms, 2.55-s cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Murugan 2013, thesis, Laurentian University, pp. 44-45 (248-point burst-x, 849-point Thomas pulse, 3-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/39c9c1ad-70ba-458d-a819-d24c20da217a ; Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999, Percept Mot Skills 89:486 (3-ms pixel and interstimulus optimum in rats) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10597585/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
